# Syscalls

<!-- Generated by scripts/gen_docs.py in kagantmr/zuzu. Do not edit. -->

Every function in `<zuzu/zuzu.h>`, grouped as in the header. Syscalls are listed by number; library helpers built on them follow each group.

## Basics

| Number | Name | Selector | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|
| `0x00` | [`Quit`](quit.md) |  | Ends the calling task. |
| `0x01` | [`Yield`](yield.md) |  | Gives up the rest of the caller's timeslice. |
| `0x02` | [`Sleep`](sleep.md) |  | Blocks the calling task for at least `ms` milliseconds. |
| `0x07` | [`WaitOn`](waiton.md) |  | Waits until `h` has something to report, or `timeout` milliseconds pass. |
| helper | [`BenchDump`](benchdump.md) |  | Prints the kernel's benchmark counters to the kernel console (CONFIG_ZUZU_BENCH builds only; a no-op otherwise). |
| helper | [`BenchReset`](benchreset.md) |  | Clears the kernel's benchmark counters (CONFIG_ZUZU_BENCH builds only; a no-op otherwise). |
| helper | [`PtrIsErr`](ptriserr.md) |  | Tells whether a pointer returned by MemMap() or MemMapAnon() is an error. |

## Handles

| Number | Name | Selector | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|
| `0x08` | [`HandleClose`](handleclose.md) | `MNGHNDL_CLOSE (2)` | Closes a handle. |
| `0x08` | [`HandleDestroy`](handledestroy.md) | `MNGHNDL_DESTROY (4)` | Closes a handle and, for a space, tears the space down. |
| `0x08` | [`HandleDuplicate`](handleduplicate.md) | `MNGHNDL_DUPLICATE (0)` | Creates a second handle to the same object, with the same or fewer permissions. |
| `0x08` | [`HandleGrant`](handlegrant.md) | `MNGHNDL_GRANT (5)` | Copies a handle into another space's handle table. |
| `0x08` | [`HandleQueryAt`](handlequeryat.md) | `MNGHNDL_QUERY (3)` | Reads one property of a handle or the object behind it. |
| `0x08` | [`HandleRestrict`](handlerestrict.md) | `MNGHNDL_RESTRICT (1)` | Removes permissions from a handle. |
| helper | [`HandleDup`](handledup.md) |  | HandleDuplicate() that stores the new handle in `out`. |
| helper | [`HandleGrantTo`](handlegrantto.md) |  | HandleGrant() that stores the target's handle value in `out`. |
| helper | [`HandleIsAlive`](handleisalive.md) |  | Tells whether a handle is live and its object has not died. |
| helper | [`HandleQuery`](handlequery.md) |  | HandleQueryAt() for properties that take no index. |
| helper | [`HandleQuerySize`](handlequerysize.md) |  | Reads the size in bytes of a memory object. |
| helper | [`HandleQueryValue`](handlequeryvalue.md) |  | HandleQuery() that stores the value in `out`. |

## Tasks

| Number | Name | Selector | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|
| `0x04` | [`CreateTask`](createtask.md) | `OBJECT_TASK (0)` | Creates a task in a space. |
| `0x0C` | [`TaskGetRegs`](taskgetregs.md) | `MNGTASK_GET_REGS (7)` | Reads the user registers of a faulted or suspended task. |
| `0x0C` | [`TaskKill`](taskkill.md) | `MNGTASK_KILL (1)` | Terminates another task, as if it had called Quit(ERR_DEAD). |
| `0x0C` | [`TaskResume`](taskresume.md) | `MNGTASK_RESUME (6)` | Lets a suspended task run again, or continues a faulted task. |
| `0x0C` | [`TaskSetMaxPriority`](tasksetmaxpriority.md) | `MNGTASK_SET_MAX_PRIO (3)` | Sets the highest priority a task may give itself; lowers its base priority if needed. |
| `0x0C` | [`TaskSetPriority`](tasksetpriority.md) | `MNGTASK_SET_PRIORITY (2)` | Sets a task's base priority. |
| `0x0C` | [`TaskSetRegs`](tasksetregs.md) | `MNGTASK_SET_REGS (8)` | Writes the user registers of a faulted or suspended task. |
| `0x0C` | [`TaskSetTimeSlice`](tasksettimeslice.md) | `MNGTASK_SET_TIMESLICE (4)` | Sets how long a task runs before same-priority tasks get a turn. |
| `0x0C` | [`TaskStart`](taskstart.md) | `MNGTASK_START (0)` | Starts a task created by CreateTask(). |
| `0x0C` | [`TaskSuspend`](tasksuspend.md) | `MNGTASK_SUSPEND (5)` | Stops a task until TaskResume(). |
| helper | [`FormatToTaskWait`](formattotaskwait.md) |  | Unpacks the registers of a WaitOn() on a task. |
| helper | [`WaitOnTask`](waitontask.md) |  | Waits for a task to exit or fault. |

## Spaces

| Number | Name | Selector | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|
| `0x04` | [`CreateSpace`](createspace.md) | `OBJECT_SPACE (1)` | Creates an empty space. |
| helper | [`FormatToSpaceWait`](formattospacewait.md) |  | Unpacks the registers of a WaitOn() on a space. |

## Memory and DMA

| Number | Name | Selector | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|
| `0x04` | [`CreateMem`](createmem.md) | `OBJECT_MEMORY (4)` | Creates a memory object that can be mapped, shared, injected and used for DMA. |
| `0x0B` | [`DmaAdopt`](dmaadopt.md) | `MNGMEM_DMAADOPT (7)` | Returns a fresh handle to the memory behind an existing DMA mapping. |
| `0x0B` | [`DmaMap`](dmamap.md) | `MNGMEM_DMAMAP (4)` | Lets a device reach part of a memory object by DMA. |
| `0x0B` | [`DmaSync`](dmasync.md) | `MNGMEM_DMASYNC (6)` | Makes cached memory and a device agree before or after a transfer. |
| `0x0B` | [`DmaUnmap`](dmaunmap.md) | `MNGMEM_DMAUNMAP (5)` | Removes a DMA mapping and releases its hold on the memory. |
| `0x0B` | [`MemInjectObj`](meminjectobj.md) | `MNGMEM_INJECTOBJ (3)` | Maps part of a memory object into another space, typically one being set up. |
| `0x0B` | [`MemMap`](memmap.md) | `MNGMEM_MAP (0)` | Maps a memory object into the caller's address space. |
| `0x0B` | [`MemMapAnon`](memmapanon.md) | `MNGMEM_MAP (0) (HANDLE_ANON)` | Maps fresh zeroed memory, backed by no object, into the caller's address space. |
| `0x0B` | [`MemProtect`](memprotect.md) | `MNGMEM_PROTECT (2)` | Changes the protection of a range of the caller's mapped memory. |
| `0x0B` | [`MemUnmap`](memunmap.md) | `MNGMEM_UNMAP (1)` | Removes a mapping made by MemMap() or MemMapAnon(). |
| helper | [`FormatToDmaMap`](formattodmamap.md) |  | Unpacks the registers of a DMA map call. |
| helper | [`MemInjectBytes`](meminjectbytes.md) |  | Copies bytes into another space at a fixed address. |

## IPC

| Number | Name | Selector | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|
| `0x04` | [`CreatePort`](createport.md) | `OBJECT_PORT (2)` | Creates a port: something callers Call() and a server receives on. |
| `0x05` | [`CallTimeout`](calltimeout.md) |  | Sends a message to a port and blocks until the server replies, or until a timeout. |
| `0x06` | [`Reply`](reply.md) |  | Answers the call the caller is holding. |
| `0x06` | [`ReplyRecv`](replyrecv.md) |  | Answers the call in hand (if any), then waits for the next one, in one syscall. |
| `0x06` | [`ReplyTo`](replyto.md) | `(ticket in r3)` | Answers a call parked with Hold(). |
| `0x0D` | [`Hold`](hold.md) |  | Parks the call in hand so the server can receive others, and returns a ticket for it. |
| helper | [`Call`](call.md) |  | Call() with no timeout: blocks until the server replies. |
| helper | [`CallPort`](callport.md) |  | Call() that stores the reply length and any granted handle. |
| helper | [`CallPortTimeout`](callporttimeout.md) |  | CallTimeout() that stores the reply length and any granted handle. |
| helper | [`FormatToPortWait`](formattoportwait.md) |  | Unpacks the registers of a receive on a port. |
| helper | [`ReplyRecvPort`](replyrecvport.md) |  | ReplyRecv() with the result unpacked. |
| helper | [`WaitOnPort`](waitonport.md) |  | Waits for a call on a port. |

## Events

| Number | Name | Selector | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|
| `0x04` | [`CreateEvent`](createevent.md) | `OBJECT_EVENT (3)` | Creates an event: 31 bits that can be signalled and waited on. |
| `0x08` | [`IrqRearm`](irqrearm.md) | `MNGHNDL_IRQ_REARM (6)` | Unmasks a device's interrupt line after BindIrq() delivered it. |
| `0x09` | [`Signal`](signal.md) |  | Sets bits on an event and wakes waiters. |
| `0x0A` | [`Bind`](bind.md) | `EVENT_PORT (3), EVENT_TASK (4), EVENT_SPACE (5)` | Has the kernel set an event bit when a port, task or space needs attention. |
| `0x0A` | [`BindIrq`](bindirq.md) | `EVENT_IRQ (2)` | Delivers a device's interrupt as an event bit. |
| `0x0A` | [`BindMemMgmt`](bindmemmgmt.md) | `EVENT_MEMMGMT (1)` | Subscribes an event to the kernel's memory-pressure notifications. |
| helper | [`FormatToEventWait`](formattoeventwait.md) |  | Unpacks the registers of a WaitOn() on an event. |
| helper | [`WaitOnEvent`](waitonevent.md) |  | Waits for bits on an event, then clears them. |
